title: Monarch: Legacy of Monsters
synopsis: Your grandfather's basement contains seventeen file cabinets, a key to a Tokyo apartment, and a black-and-white photograph of him with a Titan. You inherit it all. Try to stay alive.

nodes.text: You inherit, alongside a paid-off mortgage and a sad fish, a box of files marked MONARCH — TOP SECRET. Your half-brother you didn't know existed sits across the church.

choices.text: Introduce yourself to him
Walk past and read the files first
choices.consequence: You commit to “Walk past and read the files first.” The story records the instinct as “Information first” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Kentaro is your age, raised in Tokyo, equally surprised. He has half the photographs you have. The puzzle, you realize, was always meant to be two-handed.

choices.text: Compare files together immediately
Buy him a drink first

nodes.text: The first file is a map with a red circle around an island in the Pacific. The second is a casualty list — civilian, military, both. The third is a photograph of a creature that should not, by current physics, exist.

choices.text: Read every file before you act
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Read every file before you act” back. Discipline shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

choices.text: Take the most actionable file and move
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Speed.

nodes.text: A man in his thirties, polite, badly dressed, finds you at a coffee shop. 'Monarch wants to help,' he says. 'But you should be careful about who answers their phone right now.'

choices.text: Go with Tim to a Monarch safehouse
Refuse and run with the files

nodes.text: Inside the apartment is a phone that still works, a kettle, and a wall covered in photographs of the same family — yours, at different decades. Your grandfather kept two lives.

choices.text: Photograph the wall for the record
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Document—follows you into whatever comes next.

choices.text: Sit on the floor and let it hit you
choices.consequence: “Sit on the floor and let it hit you” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Feel it.

nodes.text: Lee Shaw — your grandfather's old partner, supposedly dead, very alive — walks out of a back room in a leather coat. He looks at you, then Kentaro, then back. He says, 'You found me before they did.'

choices.text: Trust Shaw
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Old hands.

choices.text: Verify Shaw first

nodes.text: On the wall there is a single new pin in a place that wasn't there in any other file — a pin in Kansas. Your grandfather was, somehow, tracking a Titan in Kansas. You don't know why.

choices.text: Go to Kansas
Triangulate from Tokyo first

nodes.text: A small Monarch outpost outside a town that doesn't appear on highway maps. The team here is friendly and scared. They show you a tunnel that goes very, very far down.

choices.text: Descend with them
Send Kentaro down; stay with the data
choices.consequence: You commit to “Send Kentaro down; stay with the data.” The story records the instinct as “Divide labor” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Shaw shows you a recording — Titan calls layered on top of each other. The pattern, he claims, is a language. Your grandfather had translated it partially. The files have the rest.

choices.text: Translate it together
Take the recording to a linguist friend
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Outside expert.

nodes.text: Through a Hollow Earth tunnel: a Titan. Real. Large. Calm. It looks at you the way a dog looks at someone it has decided is not a threat. Its eye is the size of a small car.

choices.text: Sit still and let it pass
Try to record its call
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Document.

nodes.text: Apex Cybernetics has, you discover, infiltrated Monarch's leadership. The company that wants to weaponize Titans is the company that just hired half your grandfather's old friends. The betrayal is, briefly, more painful than the kaiju.

choices.text: Plan to expose Apex
Plan to undermine them from inside
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Plan to undermine them from inside” back. Subversion shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: You upload your grandfather's files to a trusted journalist with a 48-hour fuse. If you're not heard from in 48, the files publish. It is the only insurance you have that isn't a Titan.

choices.text: Keep moving and rely on the fuse
Confront the saboteur in Monarch leadership

nodes.text: In a containment lab you find a small Titan — newborn, blue-eyed, frightened. Apex was going to weaponize it. The hatchling, you realize, has been responding to its mother's calls in the recordings Shaw played.

choices.text: Release the hatchling to its mother
Move it to a Monarch sanctuary

nodes.text: Monarch's old families convene a council vote — keep the files secret, or release them. Your grandfather was the swing vote a generation ago. You are, terrifyingly, the swing vote now.

choices.text: Vote for release
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Daylight.

choices.text: Vote for limited disclosure
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Vote for limited disclosure” back. Compromise shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: You and Kentaro stand at the mouth of a tunnel and watch the hatchling find its mother. The sound the mother Titan makes shakes the air. It is, somehow, joy.

choices.text: Stay in the work
Hand the work to others and go home

nodes.text: A press conference releases redacted but real information about Monarch, Titans, and Apex. The world panics for a week and then, weirdly, adjusts. Humans are good at adjusting to the impossible. They always have been.

choices.text: Take a leadership role in the new public Monarch
Step back to advisor

nodes.text: Kentaro and his mother visit your home. Your own mother, baffled, sets six places. The dinner is — given the day — startlingly ordinary. You realize the inheritance was, partly, also a family.

choices.text: Make this a regular thing
Take it one dinner at a time

nodes.text: Monarch is, in the new public era, oversight more than secrecy. Titans are policy. You have testified before three legislatures. You sleep with the fish your grandfather kept — actually his great-grandfish — on the dresser.

choices.text: Stay in the public role
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Keep going.

choices.text: Hand off and write the family book
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Hand off and write the family book” back. Document shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: You spend a year visiting every red pin on the original map. Some are empty. Some have new villages. Some have new Titans. You take photographs your grandfather would have wanted.

choices.text: Compile them into an archive
Donate the originals to a museum
choices.consequence: “Donate the originals to a museum” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Public memory.

nodes.text: You and Kentaro spend a week in the old Tokyo apartment going through the last drawers. You find the photograph he was holding the day he died — your grandmother, in a doorway, laughing. You decide which life to live next from this room.

choices.text: Stay public; the work calls
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Stay public; the work calls” back. Director's chair shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

choices.text: Go home and write the book together
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Authors.

nodes.text: You become a director of public Monarch and, in a strange way, your grandfather's apprentice fifty years late. You preside over a small office full of files that no longer have to be hidden. You like that.

You and Kentaro write a book together about the two lives of your grandfather. It is a strange book — half family memoir, half kaiju field guide. It sells, mysteriously, on every continent. Some readers cry. Some readers leave you weird voicemails. You answer most of them.
